findings.description: storage_encrypted = false means the RDS MySQL instance's storage and any snapshots are written in cleartext, exposing all database contents to anyone who obtains the underlying storage or a copied snapshot.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable endpoint (also exported via the db_endpoint output), exposing MySQL to internet-based credential brute-forcing and exploitation despite the VPC-scoped security group rule.
The master username is the predictable default 'admin', which materially eases credential guessing against a publicly reachable MySQL endpoint.

The master password comes from var.password, the same value interpolated in cleartext into EC2 user data; it is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state rather than sourced from Secrets Manager, and ignore_changes on password prevents rotation being applied.

The user_data script writes the RDS master username and var.password in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service and visible in the console and Terraform state, so any SSRF or local compromise on this PHP host leaks database master credentials.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available on an instance running a PHP application and carrying an instance profile with s3:*, ec2:* and rds:*; an SSRF would yield both the role credentials and the plaintext user data containing the DB password.
No root_block_device encryption is configured, so the volume holding the plaintext credentials file dbinfo.inc may be stored unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption is enabled.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Because the role is attached to an internet-facing web instance without IMDSv2, a compromise yields account-wide control of S3 data, EC2 (including privilege-escalation paths such as RunInstances with PassRole) and RDS.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised host an unrestricted channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so unencrypted client connections to a publicly accessible database are permitted, allowing credentials and query data to be intercepted.
